Method of Attack: named pipe hijacking (named pipe squatting) vulnerability allowing attackers to trick PsExec into re-opening a maliciously created named pipe and giving it Local System permissions
local privilege escalation allowing a non-admin process to escalate to SYSTEM if PsExec is executed locally or remotely
Impacted Systems: Windows systems running PsExec versions from 2006 to latest (last 14 years)
Attack Vector: exploitation by non-admin attacker already running code on remote computer (e.g., regular Terminal Server user, RDP session as domain user, or vulnerable unprivileged service) to elevate privileges to Local System when PsExec is used
